primitives.verbatim_quote: Primary signal = **assignment margin** in the Hungarian cost matrix: for a matched pair (i*, j*), the margin m_{j*} is the second-best minus best assignment cost (see §4).

primitives.breakdown_regime: When m_{j*} < τ_entry, triggers window creation for mask propagation.

primitives.name: Window Dispatch
primitives.verbatim_quote: A window opens when m_{j*} < τ_entry for any matched pair.

When m_{j*} falls below τ_entry, a temporal window is opened for mask propagation. This process is governed by a set of exit conditions including IoMA thresholds, which ensure mask integrity. The asymmetric decision rule allows only contradictory VOS predictions to alter track identities, preventing cascading errors. The method assumes that assignment ambiguity correlates with identity-switch risk and that VOS models can maintain identity under occlusion. The failure mode arises from incorrect seeding or persistent low-confidence assignments, leading to stale or degraded windows. The system's robustness stems from its reliance on multiple signals—margin, IoMA, gap detection, witness windows—to make informed corrections.
